svg.aria-label: AWS deployment architecture for the database migration platform
svg.title: db-migration-platform — AWS deployment architecture
svg.desc: Source network on the left holding the source database, the .dat extractor, the CDC connector and the tokenisation boundary backed by an HSM. A private AWS VPC on the right holding the S3 parts bucket, Amazon MSK, KMS, five ECS Fargate services, an Aurora cluster and observability. The two are joined by AWS Direct Connect.
svg.text: Private VPC, no internet gateway. Sensitive columns are protected before they leave the source network, and the target never holds plaintext for them.
IBM DB2 · PostgreSQL · MySQL — still serving live traffic
the confidentiality boundary: nothing downstream of this line
holds plaintext for a protected column
unwraps one data key per process, never one call per row
The extractor writes low and high watermarks to a signal
table on the source, so they travel through the same
transaction log and are ordered against the data changes.
The reconciler queries this database over the private
circuit to compare digests against the target.
AWS · VPC — PRIVATE SUBNETS ACROSS 3 AZ · NO INTERNET GATEWAY, NO NAT
ECS FARGATE · ONE TASK ROLE PER SERVICE
AMAZON AURORA · POSTGRESQL OR MYSQL · STORAGE ENCRYPTED WITH THE CMK
S3 gateway endpoint for bulk parts; interface endpoints for KMS, Secrets Manager, ECR, CloudWatch and STS.
Aurora reads parts from S3 itself, so bulk bytes never pass through a worker process. No workload has a route to the internet.
extract → object storage → native import → fenced merge
source log → connector → broker → fenced apply
every write conditional on the source LSN
unwrapped once per process, never per row
Dashed = private circuit or a path that bypasses the workers entirely
